title: The Emergency Alert
narration: At 2:06 a.m., my phone warned me not to look outside. A supposed officer knocked while alerts called him an escaped prisoner. Masked people entered houses evacuated by an earlier false warning. The officer forced my door; beneath his mask was my husband. Police found the neighbours' valuables in his van and arrested him. His phone received one final instruction asking why he had not finished the job. Every explanation I tried made the details worse, because each clue had been placed where I alone would find it. I wanted to leave immediately, but doing that would mean abandoning the only proof that any of this had happened. The silence felt deliberate, as though someone nearby was waiting for me to understand the trap before moving again. The sender was saved as Wife, but the number was not mine.
